title: Russia launches full-scale invasion of Ukraine
body:
Russia invaded Ukraine on 24 February 2022, an escalation of the Russo-Ukrainian conflict that began in 2014. In the early hours of that day, Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a "special military operation" in a televised address. He said the operation was intended to support the Russian-backed breakaway Donetsk and Luhansk republics and to "demilitarise and denazify" Ukraine. He claimed without evidence that Ukraine's government was neo-Nazi and was committing genocide.

Russian air strikes and ground forces attacked on three main axes. A northern thrust advanced from Belarus toward the capital, Kyiv. A southern thrust moved out of Russian-occupied Crimea. An eastern thrust advanced from the Donbas region toward Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city. Ukraine responded by imposing martial law, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky remained in Kyiv.

Before the invasion, Russia had assembled an estimated 169,000 to 190,000 troops near Ukraine's borders. Ukraine's armed forces numbered about 196,600 military personnel and about 102,000 paramilitary personnel, and Ukraine's total force later grew to as many as 700,000 by July 2022. The invasion became the largest and deadliest war in Europe since the Second World War and set off a wave of sanctions, arms deliveries to Ukraine and refugee movements across the continent.
